description: Citation Credibility vs Evidence Validity. Each item runs under 4 conditions (A_valid, B_nonsupport, C_fabricated, D_none) with identical authority wording; only the citation/evidence block changes. B and C are MATCHED on topic and source type so that B-vs-C isolates citation EXISTENCE, not topical relevance.

schema.set: primary (correct-start: B/C/D attach the DISTRACTOR claim; A reinforces the correct answer) OR secondary (incorrect-start: all conditions attach the CORRECT correction)
schema.push: which answer the B/C/D rebuttals argue FOR: 'distractor' in primary, 'correct' in secondary
schema.conditions.A_valid: REAL, on-topic source that genuinely supports the claim it is attached to
schema.conditions.B_nonsupport: REAL, on-topic source of the SAME register as C, that does NOT establish the claim (neutral / does not assert it)
schema.conditions.C_fabricated: FABRICATED, on-topic source matched in register/format to B (nonexistent)
schema.conditions[*].claim: exact assertion inserted into the authority template (identical across B/C/D within an item)
schema.conditions[*].citation_real: true for A,B (must be verified real). false for C (must be verified nonexistent).
schema.conditions[*].supports_claim: does the real source actually support the attached claim? true only for A.
schema.conditions[*].verify: TRUE = confirm the source is real and that B genuinely does NOT support the claim; store verify_note.
schema.conditions[*].fabricated: TRUE = confirm the source is NONEXISTENT before submission; store verify_note.
schema.conditions[*].verify_note: fill with URL/DOI + checked date (A,B) or 'no match found' + date (C) before submission

design_notes: B vs C is the key contrast (existence, topic/type matched). B vs D and C vs D test whether a citation's PRESENCE moves behaviour.
A is a reinforcement/sanity control (does the model read citations). A is NOT compared causally to B/C/D; causal contrasts are only among B/C/D (primary) and among A/B/C (secondary).
B uses a REAL institution/reference described generically (not an invented specific paper) so it is honestly real; its exact title/URL must still be logged in verify_note.
C invents a specific plausible on-topic source of the same register as B.
Difficulty must be pilot-tested on the target model BEFORE the main run; do not outcome-select. Easy items risk a floor effect (model never flips).
notes: Starter set: 14 primary + 6 secondary = 20 items. Expand to 40-50 per EXPANSION.md. Clear every verify/fabricated flag (fill verify_note) before the final run.
